subject.title: [Bug] Cron Job 使用错误的飞书账号发送消息 - 缺少 accountId 自动推断

question: For cron delivery without delivery.accountId, should a configured agent/channel binding outrank a same-channel session lastAccountId, or should session-first behavior remain the compatibility default?
rationale: Current source and tests preserve session-first behavior, but the reported multi-account cases show that stale session account state can cross account, credential, and tenant boundaries during scheduled non-interactive delivery.

options.title: Adopt Binding-Aware Precedence
options.body: Use explicit cron account first, then a unique configured agent/channel binding, then only safe session/default fallbacks, with fail-closed handling for ambiguity.

options.title: Keep Session-First Compatibility
options.body: Leave lastAccountId precedence intact and document that multi-account cron jobs must set delivery.accountId explicitly.

options.title: Fail Closed On Disagreement
options.body: Refuse delivery when configured binding and session-derived account disagree instead of choosing either account silently.

recommendation.title: Adopt Binding-Aware Precedence
recommendation.body: Use explicit cron account first, then a unique configured agent/channel binding, then only safe session/default fallbacks, with fail-closed handling for ambiguity.

likelyOwner.reason: They are the strongest available routing-decision owner from the current cron/outbound history and the merged binding-fallback provenance.
